newsitem.title: USA: CSX does not plan to raise Conrail bid.
newsitem.headline: CSX does not plan to raise Conrail bid.

text.p: The chairman of CSX Corp told a federal court that the railroad had no plans to increase its takeover offer for Conrail Inc.
"We were at our limits with that last offer," Chairman John Snow said.
Asked by Norfolk Southern Corp lawyer Steven Rothschild if he proposed to raise the bid, Snow responded, "No, I don't."
CSX and Conrail have proposed a merger that is being challenged by Norfolk Southern.
Norfolk Southern and CSX are locked in a bidding war over Conrail. Both companies raised their offers last month.

Snow testified today that there was a good chance Conrail shareholders would approve a key provision of the merger agreement with CSX. He said the chances of approval were "reasonably good" but "not assured."
"It's certainly going to be a horserace," he said.
Conrail shareholders are being asked to waive a Pennsylvania law that would essentially require CSX to pay cash for Conrail. CSX has proposed a cash and stock transaction.
A special Conrail shareholder meeting is slated for January 17.
Norfolk Southern is challenging revised terms of the CSX-Conrail merger agreement that prohibit either company from discussing a merger with any other party until 1999.
A ruling on the issue was expected later today.
